comparator.name: Maastricht Science Programme (BSc)
comparator.sourceNotes: Maastricht’s 180 EC degree combines a 30 EC core, 10 EC of general education, 110 EC of electives and a 30 EC thesis. Students build their own profile through courses, skills training and research projects. The example keeps elective choices open within the programme’s level and catalogue rules.
components: Core course in biological processes, from molecules and cells to organisms.
Core course in chemical structure, bonding, reactions and equilibria.
Core course in physical principles and mathematical problem-solving.
Introduction to Liberal Arts and Sciences
Core course in philosophy of science, research ethics, argumentation and science communication.
Core skills training in laboratory safety, experimental design, measurement and lab reporting.
Core skills training that builds on the first laboratory course through experimental design, data analysis and reporting.
Core project that integrates the first two teaching periods through a collaborative literature review and poster presentation.
Choose one 5 EC mathematics course from the approved list.
General education: humanities or social science
Choose one 5 EC humanities or social-science course from the approved list.
Elective courses in a chosen science profile
Choose fourteen courses for a science profile. In the standard 5 EC pattern, at least four are advanced and at most three introductory.
Choose eight skills modules. At least two are advanced and at most two introductory.
Choose four projects. At least one is advanced and at most one introductory.
Complete the 30 EC research thesis in the final semester. Entry requires 145 EC, with limited coursework and a project allowed to be awaiting grades.

core: Natural-science foundations: the four-course core (Introduction to Biology, Introduction to Chemistry, Introduction to Physics, Introduction to Liberal Arts and Sciences) that every student completes before choosing advanced courses, with biology, chemistry and physics profiles

Interdisciplinary natural science: a self-built science profile that combines biology, chemistry, mathematics, physics, neurosciences and interdisciplinary fields, with introductory, intermediate and advanced levels
Mathematics, statistics and data analysis: a mandatory mathematics course, mathematics and computer-science courses and the analysis of scientific data

Laboratory experiments, research skills and research projects: core and elective skills trainings, five three-week projects, laboratory work, scientific writing and the design of original research projects
Advanced and independent work: a minimum of four 3000-level courses and a 30-EC Bachelor Thesis Research in a field of the student's choice
adjacent: Neurosciences: a formally identified study direction available within the science profile
Biomedical engineering and systems biology: interdisciplinary profiles that combine biology with engineering, mathematics and computation
Chemistry, physics, biobased materials and nanomaterials: chemistry and physics profiles and the interdisciplinary materials directions
questions: How can natural science help solve scientific challenges in energy, health and sustainability?
How can original scientific research questions without known answers be investigated and reported?

trace: teaches research logic and design, experimental design, laboratory research techniques and descriptive and inferential statistics; it directly implements the experimental design and data analysis that the core research skills training develops

teaches search and optimisation methods for decision and fitting problems; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the optimisation toolkit for fitting and analysing models of biological systems

teaches algorithm design and analysis and the data structures behind efficient computation; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the computational foundation for large biological and imaging data sets
teaches data visualisation, cleaning and manipulation with hands-on science data sets; it directly implements the analysis of scientific data that the programme trains
Complementary predictive methods: regression, classification and resampling support modeling biological data.
Direct imaging methods: digital image processing and feature extraction provide transferable tools for biomedical imaging.
Complementary computational methods: neural network implementation, training and evaluation support data modeling. Artificial networks do not establish neural-circuit coverage.

teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python, including testing and debugging; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the computational skill used to analyse and model scientific data

teaches the widely used mathematical techniques, such as differentiation, that the sciences rely on; it directly implements the mathematics element of the programme, which includes a mandatory mathematics course

teaches systems of linear equations, matrices, vectors and vector spaces; it directly implements the mathematics element of the programme and supplies the linear algebra used in modelling and data analysis
teaches numerical solution of equations, differentiation and differential equations with computer algebra software; it directly implements computational mathematics for scientific problems
extends calculus to several dimensions and differential equations with computer algebra; it directly implements the mathematical modelling used in systems biology and engineering
teaches linear time-invariant systems, signals, convolution, transfer functions, state space and differential equations; it directly implements advanced mathematics for modelling dynamic systems
teaches probability theory, distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; it directly implements the statistics element of the programme at advanced level
teaches the theory of evolution and the evidence for it; it directly implements the evolutionary biology that MSP students can include in a biology profile
teaches ecology from individuals and populations to ecosystems, with ecological modelling; it directly implements the ecology and organismal biology of a biology profile

covers sustainable farming, integrated pest management, organic farming and precision agriculture; it makes a specific complementary contribution by applying biology to a sustainability challenge involving food, health and environment

introduces earth science, from surface and deep-earth processes to the physical basis of natural phenomena; it makes a specific complementary contribution that brings the physical-science side of interdisciplinary natural science into the programme, although UCR has no physics course

teaches Earth-system modelling, proxies and isotope tracers and includes a field trip on greenhouse-gas pathways; it makes a specific complementary contribution by applying quantitative modelling to Earth-system processes

focuses on biogeochemical processes at the Earth's surface, including biological and chemical controls on mineral formation and the recovery of resources; it directly implements the interface between chemistry, biology and earth science, although it is not a general chemistry course

introduces the planetary-boundaries framework and the mathematics, physics and modelling needed to study the Earth system; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the quantitative gateway to the earth and environmental science courses
covers the drivers and impacts of climate change on living and non-living Earth systems; it directly implements the energy and sustainability challenge to which the programme applies natural science

examines human anatomical structures in relation to function across body systems with dissection materials; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the structural basis for neuroscience and human biology

teaches the principles of pharmacology, drug targets and the molecular mechanisms through which drugs act on the diseased body; it makes a specific complementary contribution that links neuroscience to its biomedical applications

studies immune recognition, lymphocyte repertoires, innate and adaptive responses and host-pathogen interactions; it makes a specific complementary contribution as a second biomedical systems course, although it is not neuroscience

relates normal function to disease for six organ systems, including the central nervous system; it makes a specific complementary contribution that applies physiology and neuroscience to disease mechanisms
focuses on the biology side of neuroscience, including evolutionary pressures on behaviour, cell staining and microscopy; it directly implements the neuroscience direction

examines the neural mechanisms behind perception and action using methods of cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology; it directly implements the neuroscience direction (sensory processing and motor control)
deepens neurophysiology and neuroanatomy and the experimental approaches of cognitive neuroscience for memory, attention and executive functions; it directly implements advanced neuroscience

studies the neurobiological and psychological factors behind language, with a primary focus on the neuroscience of language; it directly implements the neuroscience direction applied to language processing

introduces the building blocks of life and how cells, molecules and systems interact to sustain living organisms; it directly implements the biology foundation that the Introduction to Biology core course provides

introduces how the brain produces behaviour and the foundations of cognitive science and neuroscience; it directly implements the neuroscience direction as the gateway to the cognitive-neuroscience courses
teaches the cell biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes and the molecular mechanisms of life processes; it directly implements the cellular and molecular biology that underlies the biology profile

teaches the normal functioning of the adult human body and its organ systems, including their chemical and physical processes; it makes a specific complementary contribution by treating the organism as an integrated physiological system, although it is human rather than general biology

teaches the chemistry of life, namely proteins, sugars, lipids, nucleic acids and metabolic pathways; it is the closest UCR content to the chemistry core but is biochemistry rather than general, organic or physical chemistry

teaches biochemical and molecular laboratory work, with laboratory methods, experimental procedures and data analysis; it directly implements the laboratory experimentation that the core research skills trainings and the programme's laboratory emphasis require
covers general and molecular pathology and the molecular genetics of human disease at 300 level; it directly implements advanced specialist work in the biology profile

teaches multivariate statistics including regression, factor analysis and ANOVA/ANCOVA for research on complex human phenomena; it directly implements the experimental and statistical research training that neuroscience requires

teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis, including effect sizes and literature review; it directly implements advanced research training for evidence synthesis in neuroscience and biomedical science
Direct Earth-systems methods: spatial analysis and integration of satellite and drone data for environmental investigations.
Direct ecology: marine habitats, ecological processes and human impacts, including field observation.

alternatives.label: Life Science, Earth Systems and Data Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: Study cells, genes and metabolism alongside evolution, marine ecology, climate and Earth systems. Use laboratory experiments, remote sensing, statistics and modeling to study biological and environmental processes. Maastricht gives more room for dedicated chemistry and physics and requires a full-semester research thesis.
alternatives.concept: Study cells, genes and metabolism alongside evolution, marine ecology, climate and Earth systems. Use laboratory experiments, remote sensing, statistics and modeling to study biological and environmental processes. Maastricht gives more room for dedicated chemistry and physics and requires a full-semester research thesis.
progression: Life science and mathematics gateways precede their dependent courses. Dynamic Earth precedes Earth Observation and Earth System Science Tools. Biochemistry and molecular cell biology precede laboratory work.

alternatives.label: Neuroscience and Biomedical Science
alternatives.labelReason: Study how the brain supports perception, cognition and language alongside the biology of health and disease. Use experimental design, statistics and systematic review to evaluate evidence. Laboratory work develops practical skills in biochemistry and molecular biology.
alternatives.concept: Study how the brain supports perception, cognition and language alongside the biology of health and disease. Use experimental design, statistics and systematic review to evaluate evidence. Laboratory work develops practical skills in biochemistry and molecular biology.
alternatives.distinctness: Neuroscience and Biomedical Science emphasises neural mechanisms, cognition, pharmacology and evidence synthesis. Compared with option 1, each plan has 13 courses the other does not.
progression: The brain and behavior gateway precedes all three dependent cognition courses. Psycholinguistics and Neurobiology run together in the only planned term for Psycholinguistics. Experimental methods precede the research seminar, and Mathematical Methods precedes the neural networks course.

alternatives.label: Life Science, Mathematical Modeling and Imaging
alternatives.labelReason: Combine cell biology, physiology and laboratory work with mathematical modeling, machine learning and image analysis. Linear systems and numerical methods provide tools for studying signals and dynamic processes. Maastricht offers dedicated biomedical engineering and systems biology electives beyond this plan.
alternatives.concept: Combine cell biology, physiology and laboratory work with mathematical modeling, machine learning and image analysis. Linear systems and numerical methods provide tools for studying signals and dynamic processes. Maastricht offers dedicated biomedical engineering and systems biology electives beyond this plan.
alternatives.distinctness: Life Science, Mathematical Modeling and Imaging emphasises numerical modeling, image processing, machine learning and algorithms. Compared with option 1, each plan has 11 courses the other does not. Compared with option 2, each plan has 7 courses the other does not.
traceOverrides: examines human anatomical structures in relation to function across body systems; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the anatomical basis for biomedical engineering and imaging

relates normal function to disease for six organ systems; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the physiological and pathological systems that biomedical engineering and systems biology model

focuses on the biology side of neuroscience, including neural systems and microscopy; it makes a specific complementary contribution as neural-systems biology for systems biology, although it is not computational neuroscience
teaches multivariate statistics including regression, factor analysis and ANOVA/ANCOVA; it directly implements the statistical modelling of biomedical and biological data
covers the theory and Python implementation of neural networks and deep learning; it directly implements machine learning for biomedical signals and images
progression: Life-science, programming and mathematics foundations precede their dependent courses. Introductory data science precedes imaging and machine learning.

candidates.label: Chemistry, physics, biobased materials and nanomaterials

selection.assessment: The closest option combines experimental life science with Earth systems, ecology and quantitative analysis. Neuroscience has its own brain, cognition and biomedical sequence. The third option adds sustained modeling and imaging methods to biological foundations. Pairwise differences are 1/2: 13 courses each way, 1/3: 11 courses each way, 2/3: 7 courses each way. Sustainability Essentials I and Environmental Biogeochemistry substantively address applied physical and chemical principles, but available courses do not build the general chemistry, physics and materials depth needed for a separate direction. UCR offers laboratory and analytical preparation for independent work, and optional independent research outside the plans.

Both introduce the biology of living systems. UCR emphasizes molecules, cells and human biology.
Maastricht introduces general chemistry. UCR Biochemistry covers chemical processes in living organisms.
Maastricht requires introductory physics. UCR applies selected physical principles in sustainability and Earth science courses.
Ecology, Earth system and sustainability science
Mathematics, statistics, data science and computing
Laboratory skills, research methods and research projects
Both develop experimental skills. UCR’s laboratory course emphasizes biochemical and molecular methods.
Both develop experimental design and data analysis. Maastricht applies them in a dedicated laboratory skills course.
Maastricht integrates the core courses through a collaborative literature review and poster presentation.
Maastricht teaches philosophy and communication of science in a dedicated course.
Personal development, general education, elective space and thesis
Maastricht requires one mathematics choice. UCR develops mathematics across several scheduled courses.
Maastricht requires one approved humanities or social-science course.
Maastricht students choose courses for their own science profile. The three UCR plans illustrate distinct combinations.
Maastricht students choose eight additional skills modules. UCR teaches related methods within its scheduled courses.
Maastricht students complete four additional research projects in dedicated project periods.
Maastricht requires a 30 EC thesis. UCR independent research is optional and sits outside the scheduled degree.

notes.text: Maastricht requires dedicated introductory chemistry and physics and offers specialist electives in both. The UCR plans draw on related principles in biochemistry, Earth science and sustainability. They also develop biology, laboratory work and quantitative methods.

Maastricht combines a fixed science core with a self-designed profile, recurring skills modules and research projects, and a 30 EC thesis. UCR develops related methods within scheduled courses and offers optional independent research separately.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht’s English-taught science bachelor combines biology, chemistry and physics with laboratory training. Students design a profile and finish with a research thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Maastricht curriculum shows the 2026–2027 requirements and leaves elective choices open. The published 2025–2026 catalogue illustrates what core courses cover. The three UCR plans illustrate life and Earth science, neuroscience, and quantitative approaches to life science.
